newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian T-bills open flat in very quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Canadian T-bills open flat in very quiet trade.

text.p: Canadian T-bills open little changed in very quiet trade on Monday with the market largely focused on U.S. data out later this week, dealers said.

"It's the same prices we were looking at on Friday at the close, almost right out through the whole entire short end," said one dealer with a bank-owned brokerage. "There's a lot of data coming out for the market this week, especially south of the border."
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill traded unchanged from Friday's close to yield 3.25 percent.

Dealers said the Canadian money market was very quiet, with many investors waiting to see how this week's U.S. data affects bond markets. Key reports out this week include the U.S. retail sales report for July on Wednesday and the consumer price index for July on Thursday.
In other prices, the six-month when-issued T-bill weakened to yield 3.71 percent from 3.70 percent on Friday. The one-year when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 4.13 percent from 4.15 percent.
The call loan or overnight lending rate traded at 3.30 percent, near the center of the Bank of Canada's 3.0-3.5 percent target range.
